identities.label: Kingdom of Mrauk U
identities.summary: The Kingdom of Mrauk-U (Arakanese: မြောက်ဦး ဘုရင့်နိုင်ငံတော်) or Kingdom of Arakan was a kingdom that existed on the Arakan coastal plain from 1429 to 1785. Based in the capital Mrauk U, near the eastern coast of the Bay of Bengal, the kingdom ruled over what is now Rakhine State, Myanmar, and the southern part of Chittagong Division, Bangladesh. Though it started out as a protectorate of the Bengal Sultanate from 1429 to 1531, Mrauk-U went on to conquer Chittagong with the help of the Portuguese. It twice fended off the Toungoo Burma's attempts to conquer the kingdom in 1546–1547, and 1580–1581.

Q10330186.label: Min Razagyi
Q10330186.summary: Min Razagyi (Arakanese and Burmese: မင်းရာဇာကြီး, Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ ɹàzà ɡɹí], Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ jàzà dʑí]; c. 1557–1612; also spelled as Mang Raza Gree), was king of Arakan from 1593 to 1612. His early reign marked the continued ascent of the coastal kingdom, which reached full flight in 1599 by defeating its nemesis Toungoo dynasty, and temporarily controlling the Bay of Bengal coastline from the Sundarbans to the Gulf of Martaban until 1603. But the second half of his reign saw the limits of his power: he lost the Lower Burmese coastline in 1603 and a large part of Bengal coastline in 1609 due to insurrections by Portuguese mercenaries.

Q16873158.label: Nara Apaya
Q16873158.summary:
Nara Apaya  (Burmese: နရအဘယ; 1694 - 28 October 1761) was a 41st king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan from 1743 until his death in 1761. Born from a poor background, he inherited the throne from his nephew. 
He was the longest reigning monarch of Mrauk-U, of the last period.
During his reign, the country faced severe economic and political crisis that in order to solve, the king launched military campaign against the neighboring countries.

Q19660890.label: Sanda Thudhamma
Q19660890.summary: Sanda Thudhamma Raza (Arakanese: စန္ဒသုဓမ္မရာဇာ, February 1637 - 20 December 1684) was 24th king of the Mrauk U Kingdom. He reigned from 1652 to 1674. He lost the control of Chittagong during his reign and the Dutch VOC left in 1664 following their trade agreement in 1653. Due to the loss of Chittagong, the kingdom began to declined and isolated after his death in 1684.

Q4779254.label: Apaya
Q4779254.summary: Apaya Maha Raza (Arakanese:အဘယ မဟာရာဇာ, 1710 - 17 January 1774)  was the 44th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma). from 1764 to 1774. The king's son, crown prince who rose in rebellion died by his own hand. He was succeeded by his brother-in-law after successful revolt whom the king died.

Q4837068.label: Ba Saw Nyo
Q4837068.summary: Ba Saw Nyo (Burmese: ဘစောညို, pronounced [ba̰ sɔ́ ɲò]; 1435–1494) was king of Arakan from 1492 to 1494. The king is known for erecting a small stupa called Radanar Hmankin in 1492. The king was also referred to as Muhammad Shah by the neighbouring Bengal.

Q4837069.label: Ba Saw Phyu
Q4837069.summary: Ba Saw Phyu (Burmese: ဘစောဖြူ, Burmese pronunciation: [ba̰ sɔ́ pʰjù]; also spelled Ba Saw Pru, Arakanese pronunciation: [ba̰ sɔ́ pʰɹù]; 1430–1482) was king of Arakan from 1459 to 1482. He acquired Chittagong in 1459, and put down a rebellion there in 1481. He was also known as Kalima Shah by the neighbouring Bengal. He established religious contacts with Ceylon and built the Mahabodhi Shwe-Gu Temple.

Q5276537.label: Dikkha
Q5276537.summary: Min Dikkha (Burmese: မင်းတိက္ခာ, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ deiʔ kʰà]; 1515–1556, in the Arakanese language as Mong Tikkha) was ruler of the Kingdom of Mrauk U, in what is now Rakhine State, Myanmar (Burma), from 1554 to 1556. He was the heir-apparent of the kingdom for 22 years during the reign of his father, King Min Bin. Dikkha was an able military commander who led the Arakanese navy in Min Bin's conquest of Bengal in 1532–1533. He led the Royal Arakanese Navy in the Taungoo–Ava War (1538–45), and in the Taungoo–Mrauk-U War (1545–47).

Q5529018.label: Gazapati
Q5529018.summary: Gazapati (Burmese: ဂဇာပတိ, pronounced [ɡəzàpətḭ]; c. 1497–1515) was king of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma), from 1513 to 1515.

Q6350348.label: Kalamandat
Q6350348.summary: Kalamandat  (Burmese: ကာလဗန္ဒလ, my, Arakanese pronunciation: my;) was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma). He was originally a monk.

Q6726518.label: Madarit
Q6726518.summary: Madarit (Arakanese:မေတ္တရစ်,1718 - 6 January 1743) was a 40th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma).

Q6732672.label: Maha Thammada of Mrauk-U
Q6732672.summary:
Maha Thammada (Rakhine: မဟာသမ္မတ; c. May 1742 – 1786), born Thado Aung (Rakhine: သတိုးအောင်), was the final monarch of the Kingdom of Mrauk U, reigning from 1782 to 1785. He was the last Arakanese monarch and 48th king of Mrauk-U, a coastal area of Arakan and a former state in Myanmar. 
When Sanda Thaditha died in 1782, nobles gathered and enthroned Thado Aung, who was a Duke of Ramree, held the post of Letwemyan (Burmese: လက်ဝဲမြန် အမတ်) and was the nephew-in-law of deceased King Sanda Thaditha. Thado Aung assumed the title of Maha Thammada Raza and ascended the throne, with his Queen Saw Mae Pon (Burmese: စောမယ်ပုံ).

Q6798099.label: Mayuppiya
Q6798099.summary: Mayuppiya (Arakanese: မာရုမ္ပိယ) was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He was originally a monk at Shittaung Temple.

Q6862522.label: Min Bin
Q6862522.summary: Min Bin (Arakanese and Burmese: မင်းဘင်, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɰ̃ bɪ̀ɰ̃], Arakanese pronunciation: [máɰ̃ bàɰ̃]; also known as Min Ba-Gyi (မင်းဗာကြီး, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɰ̃ bàjí], Meng Ba-Gri, Arakanese pronunciation: [máɰ̃ bà ɡɹí]); 1493–1554) was a king of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma), from 1531 to 1554, "whose reign witnessed the country's emergence as a major power". Aided by Portuguese mercenaries and their firearms, his powerful navy and army pushed the boundaries of the kingdom deep into Bengal, where coins bearing his name and styling him sultan were struck, and even interfered in the affairs of mainland Burma. He carried the esteemed title "Lord of the White Umbrella" (ထီးဖြူရှင်). He was additionally known as Zabuk Shah by the neighbouring Bengal.

Q6862528.label: Min Dawlya
Q6862528.summary: Min Dawlya (Burmese: မင်းဒေါလျာ, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ dɔ́ l̥à], Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ dɔ́ l̥à]; also known as Mathu Shah; (1456–1492) was king of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma), from 1482 to 1492.

Q6862550.label: Min Khamaung
Q6862550.summary: Min Khamaung (Arakanese: မင်းခမောင်း; Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ kʰa̰ máʊɴ], Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ kʰa̰ máʊɴ]; 1557 – c. May 1622) was king of Mrauk-U Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma), from 1612 to 1622.

Q6862552.label: Min Khayi
Q6862552.summary:
Min Khayi (Burmese: မင်းခရီ, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ kʰəjì]; also spelled Mang Khari, Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ kʰəɹì]; 1392–1459), also known as Ali Khan or Naranu (နရနု), was the second king of the Mrauk-U Kingdom from 1433 to 1459. His 25-year reign brought much needed stability to the Arakan littoral, and prepared his nascent kingdom for future expansions by his successors
He began his reign as a vassal of the Bengal Sultanate, and successfully unified the entire Arakan coastline (present-day Rakhine State in Myanmar (Burma)) in 1437. He then took full advantage of the political turmoil in Bengal by seizing Ramu, the southernmost territory of his erstwhile overlord, and raiding as far north as Chittagong. In 1455, his kingdom finally achieved recognition by Ava, which had long interfered in the affairs of Arakan, as a sovereign state.

Q6862571.label: Min Phalaung
Q6862571.summary: Min Phalaung (Burmese: မင်းဖလောင်း, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ pʰəláʊɴ]; also spelled Min Hpalaung; 27 February 1535 – 4 July [O.S. 24 June] 1593) was king of Arakan from 1572 to 1593.

Q6862573.label: Min Ran Aung
Q6862573.summary: Min Ran Aung (Burmese: မင်းရန်အောင်, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ jàɴ ʔàʊɴ]; Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ ɹàɴ ʔàʊɴ]; 1485–1494) was king of Arakan for six months in 1494. The eldest son of King Dawlya was only 8 when he was put on the throne by the ministers after his granduncle King Ba Saw Nyo's death. The ministers also married the young boy to Saw Shin Saw, daughter of Ba Saw Nyo and his cousin. Still a child, the king had no interest in governing and spent much of the time playing.

Q6862574.label: Min Raza of Mrauk-U
Q6862574.summary: Min Raza (Burmese: မင်းရာဇာ, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ jàzà]; Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ ɹàzà]; 1480–1514) was king of Arakan from 1502 to 1513. He was the father of King Min Bin (r. 1531–1554). His reign saw Arakanese first contact with the Portuguese.

Q6862581.label: Min Sanay
Q6862581.summary: Min Sanay also called Man Cane (Rakhine: မင်းစနီ, Burmese: မင်းစနေ), was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan who reigned for less than one month in 1638. He is last king of royal bloodline of Mrauk-U through house of Saw Mon.

Q6862582.label: Min Saw Hla
Q6862582.summary: Min Saw Hla (Burmese: မင်းစောလှ, [mɪ́ɴ sɔ́ l̥a̰]; 1532–1564) was king of Arakan a former state in Myanmar (Burma), from 1556 to 1564. At accession, he made his first wife Saw Bon-Htut the chief queen but also married his father's chief queen Saw Thanda. He ordered a massive building program which built and repaired dams and irrigation canals as well as improved the defenses of Mrauk-U and other key towns around the kingdom. In 1561, he commissioned the building of Htukkanthein Temple.

Q6862585.label: Min Saw Mon
Q6862585.summary:
Narameikhla Min Saw Mon, (Arakanese:နရမိတ်လှ မင်းစောမွန်, Burmese pronunciation: [nəɹa̰ meiʔl̥a̰ mɪ́ɰ̃ sɔ́  mʊ̀ɰ̃], Arakanese transliteration: Mong Saw Mwan, or Mawn Saw Mwen, Arakanese pronunciation: [mɔ́ɰ̃ sɔ́ mʊ̀aɰ̃]; 1380–1433) was the last king of the Launggyet Dynasty and the founder of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan, a former state in Myanmar (Burma).
He became king in 1404 but was driven out of Launggyet in 1406 by Crown Prince Minye Kyawswa of Ava. He sought refuge in the Bengal Sultanate, and later entered the military service of Sultan Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah. In 1429, he reclaimed the Arakanese throne with the help of the sultan, and ruled the kingdom.

Q6862588.label: Min Saw O
Q6862588.summary: Min Saw O (Burmese: မင်းစောအို, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴ sɔ́ ò]; Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ sɔ́ ò]; 1456–1515) was king of Arakan for six months in 1515. He was a brother of King Salingathu (r. 1494–1502).

Q6862593.label: Min Sekkya
Q6862593.summary: Min Sekkya (Burmese: မင်းစကြာ, [mɪ́ɴ sɛʔtɕà], Rakhine pronunciation: [máɴ sɔʔkɹà]; 1536–1572) was king of Arakan from 1564 to 1572. He succeeded his elder half-brother King Min Saw Hla, who had chosen him to be the heir apparent. The northern vassal of Tripura, which had submitted to Min Saw Hla, revolted and for a time, he lost control of Chittagong. He took back the city, but he was unsuccessful in regaining control of Tripura.

Q6867827.label: Minkhaung of Mrauk-U
Q6867827.summary: Minkhaung of Mrauk-U (Burmese: မင်းခေါင်, Burmese pronunciation: [mɪ́ɴɡàʊɴ], Arakanese pronunciation: [máɴ ɡàʊɴ]; 1477–1531) was king of Arakan from 1521 to 1531. He was a son of King Dawlya (r. 1482–1492), and succeeded his elder brother King Thazata. He ascended the throne and married his brother's chief queen, Saw Nan-Hset.

Q6936074.label: Muni Thudhammaraza
Q6936074.summary: Muni Thudhammaraza  was a 27th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q6965267.label: Naradipati
Q6965267.summary: Naradipati (Arakanese:နရဓိပတိ, 1676 - 17 June 1700)  whose personal name was Maung Phyu (မောင်ဖြူ), was a 33rd king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q6965268.label: Naradipati II
Q6965268.summary: Naradipati II (Arakanese:နရဓိပတိကြီး;  was a 37th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q6965387.label: Narapati of Mrauk-U
Q6965387.summary:
Narapati of Mrauk U (Rakhine: နာရပတိ (မြောက်ဦး)); whose personal name Nga-Kuthala (Rakhine: ငကုသလ), was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He was a great-grandson of Min Bin.
The Yatra Bell, which was believed to protect the Rakhine people, was created during the reign of King Narapati.

Q6965389.label: Narapawara
Q6965389.summary: Narapawara (Arakanese:နရပဝရ,  was a 38th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q6982960.label: Nawrahta of Mrauk-U
Q6982960.summary: Nawrahta of Mrauk-U (Rakhine: ငတုံနော်ရတာ, also known as Noratha) was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He was a child king who briefly reigned for a few days in 1696.

Q7404711.label: Salingathu
Q7404711.summary: Salingathu (Burmese: စလင်္ကာသူ [səlìɴɡəθù], 1455–1502), was King of Arakan from 1494 to 1502.

Q7415920.label: Sanda Parama
Q7415920.description: king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan
Q7415920.summary:
Sanda Parama (Arakanese:စန္ဒပရမ, 1741- 1764) was a 43rd king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. Under his reign, the 1762 Arakan earthquake that destroyed much of infrastructure and agricultural lands of Arakan led to the dethroning of the king. He entered monkhood and exiled to Myingun Island.
During his short reign, the earthquake of 1762 damaged much of Arakan's agricultural production that ultimately caused great famine and political turmoil which eventually turned to regional revolts in planning to overthrown dynasty headed by the Lord of Ramree and governor of Launggyet, and the general of Cheduba Island where they asked for aid of Burmese King, Naungdawgyi.

Q7415923.label: Sanda Thaditha
Q7415923.summary: Sanda Thaditha,  (Arakanese:စန္ဒသတိဿ, 1727 - 2 November 1782) whose personal name was Aung Sone (အောင်စုန်), was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. Unlike the previous kings of Arakan, Sanda Thaditha was a native of Ramree Island.

Q7415924.label: Sanda Thumana
Q7415924.summary: Sanda Thumana (Rakhine:စန္ဒာသုမန; , whose personal name was Ngathaukkya (ငသောကြာ), was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He was unable to rule the kingdom well and many rebellions occurred during his reign.

Q7415925.label: Sanda Thuriya I
Q7415925.description: king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan
Q7415925.summary:
Sanda Thuriya I (Rakhine:စန္ဒာသူရိယရာဇာ, 1672 - 4 August 1696) whose personal name was Thado Aung Kyaw (သတိုးအောင်ကျော်), was a 28th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. Who was originally a governor of Sandoway served under during his brother's reign. The royal court enthroned him after subsequent dethroning of kings. 
He was killed by his close bodyguards after quelling the rebellion near the Kaladan River.

Q7415927.label: Sanda Thuriya II
Q7415927.description: king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan
Q7415927.summary: Sanda Thuriya II (Rakhine:စန္ဒာသူရိယ, 1660 - September 1710)  whose personal name was Thado Hla (သတိုးလှ), was a 34th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. During his reign, king of Ava tried to annex Sandoway, was successfully fend off by the governor of Sandoway, to whom sent plenty of war booties to the king.

Q7415929.label: Sanda Thuriya III
Q7415929.description: king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan
Q7415929.summary: Sanda Thuriya III (Rakhine:စန္ဒာသူရိယ, 1695 - 1734) was a 36th monarch of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q7415931.label: Sanda Wimala I
Q7415931.summary: Sanda Wimala I (Arakanese:စန္ဒာဝိမလ,  was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He was initially defeated by colliation of rebels, fled to Bengal and died.

Q7415932.label: Sanda Wimala II
Q7415932.description: king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan
Q7415932.summary: Sanda Wimala II,  whose personal name was Poe Shwe (ပိုးရွှေ), was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q7415933.label: Sanda Wizala
Q7415933.summary: Sanda Wizala (Arakanes:စန္ဒာဝိဇလ; was a 39th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q7415934.label: Sanda Wizaya
Q7415934.summary: Sanda Wizaya  (Rakhine: စန္ဒာဝီဇရ; 1665 – April 1731), commonly known as Thaungnyo, was the 35th king of the Mrauk U Dynasty of Arakan from 1710 to 1731. His reign re-established Arakan's military might for some time, raiding in the east against Mindon and Prome and in the west against Bengal. His naval fleet later sunk near Kyaukpandu upon arrival from Chittagong. He was assassinated in 1731 and succeeded by his son-in-law.

Q7709037.label: Thado of Mrauk-U
Q7709037.summary: Thado of Mrauk-U (Arakanese:သတိုးမင်းတရား,  was a king of the Mrauk-U Kingdom of Arakan from 1645 to 1652.

Q7711579.label: Thazata
Q7711579.summary: Thazata (Burmese: သဇာတ, Burmese pronunciation: [θəzàta̰]; 1464–1521) was king of Arakan from 1515 to 1521. He was a son of King Dawlya (r. 1482–1492), and governor of Ramree when he was selected by the ministers to succeed King Saw O. He moved the palace from Mrauk-U to a place called Daingkyi. He died in 1521.

Q7785101.label: Thiri Thudhamma
Q7785101.summary: Thiri Thudhamma also called Srisudhammaraja (Arakanese:သီရိသုဓမ္မ; c. April 1602 - 31 May 1638) whose personal name was Min Hari (မင်းဟရီ) was a king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.

Q7785103.label: Thiri Thuriya
Q7785103.summary: Ugga-bala (Arakanese:ဥဂ္ဂါဗလာ),  was the 25th king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He succeeded his father, Sanda Thudhamma after his death in 1684.

Q7785107.label: Thirithu
Q7785107.summary: Thirithu (Arakanese:သီရီသု,  whose personal name was Shwe Yauk (ရွှေယောက်), was a 42nd king of the Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan. He died of smallpox 3 months later after becoming king.

Q7968756.label: Wara Dhammaraza
Q7968756.summary: Wara Dhammaraza (Arakanese:ဝရ ဓမ္မာရာဇာ) was a 26th king of Mrauk-U Dynasty of Arakan.
